what_its_for: Desipramine is an antidepressant medicine used to treat depression. It belongs to a group of medicines called tricyclic antidepressants. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other conditions such as nerve pain, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), or to help with certain types of anxiety.
how_to_take: Take desipramine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a small snack or meal. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause unpleasant withdrawal symptoms like nausea, headache, and feeling unwell. Your doctor will slowly lower your dose when it is time to stop.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time to find the dose that works best for you. Most adults start with 25 mg to 100 mg per day, which may be increased up to 300 mg per day if needed. You may take your total daily dose as one dose at bedtime or split it into smaller doses throughout the day. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store desipramine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely by using a drug take-back program or mixing it with an undesirable substance like coffee grounds in a sealed bag before throwing it in the trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking desipramine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may worsen depression. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can cause drowsiness. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as desipramine can cause dizziness or lightheadedness when you change positions. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight or tanning beds, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to the sun — use sunscreen and wear protective clothing. Avoid taking other medicines, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements, without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many medicines interact with desipramine. In particular, never take MAO inhibitor medicines (such as phenelzine, tranylcypromine, or selegiline) within 14 days of taking desipramine, as this combination can be life-threatening.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or harming yourself, new or worsening depression or anxiety, sudden changes in mood or behavior, chest pain or a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, difficulty urinating, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), severe constipation, high fever with sweating and confusion, or seizures. Contact your doctor as soon as possible if you notice: increased nervousness or restlessness, dry mouth that does not improve, blurred vision, unusual weight gain or loss, trembling or shaking, or skin rash. All patients, especially those under age 25, should be watched closely for unusual changes in mood or behavior, especially during the first few weeks of treatment or when the dose is changed.
when_it_works: Desipramine does not work right away. You may start to notice some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy within the first 1 to 2 weeks. However, it usually takes 4 to 6 weeks of regular use to feel the full benefits for depression. Some people may need up to 8 weeks before they see the full effect. It is very important to keep taking your medicine even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Children and teenagers: Desipramine is generally not recommended for children under 12 years of age. In children and young adults up to age 24, there is an increased risk of suicidal thoughts, especially at the start of treatment. Parents and caregivers should watch young patients closely for mood changes or unusual behavior and report any concerns to the doctor immediately. Older adults (65 and older): Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of desipramine, especially dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, and confusion. Doses are usually started lower and increased slowly. There is also a higher risk of falls due to dizziness. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Desipramine should only be used during pregnancy if your doctor decides the benefit outweighs the risk. It may pass into breast milk, so discuss the risks and benefits of breastfeeding with your doctor. Heart conditions: Tell your doctor if you have any heart problems, as desipramine can affect heart rhythm. Your doctor may order an electrocardiogram (EKG) before and during treatment.
